abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems by improving the integration of dense retrieval methods with generative architectures. We propose a novel framework that introduces a dual-encoder retrieval mechanism coupled with a transformer-based generation model, optimized for factual consistency. Our approach integrates an iterative retrieval strategy that refines the retrieval set dynamically based on intermediate generation outputs, thus enhancing factual grounding. We evaluate our method on a suite of knowledge-intensive tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in factual accuracy and relevance over existing baselines. Our contributions include a new architecture for retrieval-generation fusion, a method for handling noisy retrievals, and a comprehensive evaluation methodology for factual grounding in RAG systems.

contributions.title: Dual-Encoder Retrieval Mechanism
contributions.description: Introduces a dual-encoder model for dense retrieval that improves retrieval quality by capturing both query and context representations.
contributions.novelty: This mechanism utilizes a novel cross-attention layer between encoders to enhance semantic alignment, improving retrieval performance compared to single-encoder models.

contributions.title: Iterative Retrieval-Generation Fusion
contributions.description: Develops an iterative strategy that refines retrievals based on intermediate generation outputs, ensuring better factual alignment.
contributions.novelty: Unique in its feedback loop design, allowing the system to self-correct and refine retrievals iteratively, unlike traditional one-pass systems.

contributions.title: Noise-Resilient Generation
contributions.description: Incorporates a noise-handling module that identifies and mitigates the impact of irrelevant or contradictory documents in the retrieval set.
contributions.novelty: Employs a dynamic weighting scheme that adjusts the influence of each retrieved document based on its relevance and consistency with generated content.

methodology.problemFormulation: The task is to improve the factual consistency and relevance of generated content in RAG systems by refining the retrieval and fusion processes.
methodology.approach: Our approach combines a dual-encoder dense retrieval model with a transformer-based generation model. We introduce iterative retrieval refinement and a noise-resilient generation module to enhance factual accuracy.

components.name: Dual-Encoder Model
components.role: Retrieves contextually relevant documents using separate encoders for query and context.
components.details: Utilizes cross-attention between query and context encoders to enhance retrieval specificity.

components.name: Transformer Generator
components.role: Generates responses based on retrieved documents.
components.details: Incorporates a feedback loop to refine retrievals iteratively, enhancing factual grounding.

components.name: Noise-Handling Module
components.role: Mitigates the impact of noisy documents.
components.details: Assigns dynamic weights to retrieved documents based on their relevance and consistency.

assumptions: Assumes access to a large-scale, high-quality retrieval corpus.
Assumes that iterative refinement will converge to optimal retrieval sets.
limitations: Increased computational cost due to iterative retrieval and generation.
Dependence on the quality of initial retrievals for effective refinement.

evidence.description: Evaluates factual accuracy improvements on a knowledge-intensive QA dataset.

evaluation.protocol: Compare factual correctness and relevance of answers generated by baseline and proposed systems.

results.notes: Proposed system outperformed the baseline by 0.12 points.
Showed a 10% improvement in relevance over the baseline.

evidence.analysis: Results indicate significant improvements in both factual accuracy and relevance, validating the effectiveness of the proposed iterative retrieval strategy.

works.summary: Introduced dense passage retrieval models improving retrieval precision via BERT-based embeddings.
Proposed the RAG model combining retrieval and generation for improved knowledge-intensive tasks.
Explored methods to ensure factual consistency in generated text using external knowledge.

futureWork.motivation: To reduce computational costs associated with iterative retrieval while maintaining accuracy.
To extend the capabilities of RAG systems to support multilingual knowledge bases and queries.
